prompts.teamwork.agenda.detailed: Draft a meeting agenda. Topic: [topic]. Goal — what should be decided by the end: [goal]. Length: [minutes] minutes. Participants by role: [roles]. Items with timings, who leads each (by role), the result needed for each. Finish with 5 minutes for summary and next steps.
prompts.teamwork.agenda.refine: The meeting's been cut to [minutes] minutes. What stays and what moves to chat?
prompts.teamwork.agenda.check: For each agenda item: does it need a meeting, or would a message do?
prompts.teamwork.decisions.short: Pull the decisions out of these meeting notes: [notes]
prompts.teamwork.decisions.detailed: From the meeting notes, pull out: decisions made, tasks (what, who by role, deadline), open questions that weren't agreed. If it's unclear whether something was decided, put it under open questions. Don't add anything. Notes: [notes]
prompts.teamwork.decisions.refine: Format this as a short message for the team chat.
prompts.teamwork.decisions.check: Which tasks have no owner or deadline?
prompts.teamwork.roles.short: What roles does the project [project] need for a team of [number]?
prompts.teamwork.roles.detailed: Project: [project]. Team: [number] people, strengths: [skills, no names]. Suggest roles: title, responsibilities, skills needed, who the role works with most. Suggest an allocation but leave the decision to the team. Keep the workload roughly even.
prompts.teamwork.roles.refine: One person can only give half as much time. How should we redistribute?
prompts.teamwork.roles.check: Here's how we split the roles: [roles]. Are there tasks nobody owns?
prompts.teamwork.polite.short: Make this message more polite without changing its meaning: [message]
prompts.teamwork.polite.detailed: I need to write to [who, by role] about [situation]. What I want: [goal]. My draft: [message]. Rewrite it politely and clearly: greeting, the point in the first two sentences, a specific request, a deadline if needed. No more than 6 sentences. Keep my tone, no corporate jargon.
prompts.teamwork.polite.refine: Make it shorter, for a messenger app.
prompts.teamwork.polite.check: How might someone in a bad mood read this? What might sting?
prompts.teamwork.help.short: Help me ask [who, by role] for help with [task].
prompts.teamwork.help.detailed: Help me write a request for help. To: [who, by role]. With: [task]. What I've already tried: [what I tried]. What exactly I need: [what I need]. The message should show I value their time: get to the point, ask a specific question, offer “if it's not convenient, could you point me to someone else”.
prompts.teamwork.help.refine: Make a version for someone I haven't talked to before.
prompts.teamwork.help.check: Could my request be answered in 5 minutes? If not, how can I simplify it?
prompts.teamwork.feedback.short: Help me phrase feedback on some work: [what's wrong]
prompts.teamwork.feedback.detailed: I need to give feedback on [what the work is]. What went well: [good]. What needs fixing: [fix]. Phrase it neutrally: specific observations instead of judgements, the effect on the result, a suggestion or question about how to improve. No “always”, “never” or comments on personality.
prompts.teamwork.feedback.refine: Make a version for saying in person rather than writing.
prompts.teamwork.feedback.check: Here's how I want to say it: [text]. Where does it sound like blame?
prompts.teamwork.disagree.short: How can I disagree with [proposal] without blaming anyone?
prompts.teamwork.disagree.detailed: The team is proposing: [proposal]. I disagree because [reason]. Help me write a reply: acknowledge what's sensible in the proposal, state my concerns in terms of facts and consequences, offer an alternative or a way to test it, and ask for others' views. No sarcasm or “you don't understand”.
prompts.teamwork.disagree.refine: Make it softer: I'm the most junior and don't want to sound harsh.
prompts.teamwork.disagree.check: What are the strongest arguments on the other side? I want to take them into account.
prompts.teamwork.summary.short: Write a meeting summary from these notes: [notes]
prompts.teamwork.summary.detailed: Write a meeting summary for those who couldn't attend. Structure: what was discussed (2–3 sentences), what was decided, who does what by when (by role), what's still open, when the next meeting is. No unnecessary detail and no blow-by-blow of debates. Notes: [notes]
prompts.teamwork.summary.refine: Shorten it to 5 lines for a messenger.
prompts.teamwork.summary.check: Is there anything in the summary that could be read two ways?
prompts.teamwork.open.short: Which questions are still open in this discussion: [notes]?
prompts.teamwork.open.detailed: Read the discussion and list the open questions: what wasn't agreed, what needs more information, who should decide (by role). For each: how urgent, what it's blocking, and how to close it (find out, vote, ask a manager). Discussion: [notes]
prompts.teamwork.open.refine: Rephrase question [number] so it can be answered briefly.
prompts.teamwork.open.check: Which question, if left unresolved, would hurt the project most?
prompts.teamwork.recipient.short: Rewrite this message for [recipient, by role]: [message]
prompts.teamwork.recipient.detailed: The same news needs to go to different people: [news]. Make 3 versions: for [recipient 1], for [recipient 2], for [recipient 3] (by role). For each consider: what they need to know, how much detail, what tone suits. The facts stay the same in all.
prompts.teamwork.recipient.refine: Make the version for [recipient] more formal.
prompts.teamwork.recipient.check: Will [recipient] understand from the message what's expected of them?

verify.teamwork.agenda: Share the agenda with participants in advance: they may add something important you didn't know about.
verify.teamwork.decisions: Send the decision list to participants: mistakes get spotted faster that way.
verify.teamwork.roles: Discuss roles with the team: people know their own strengths and workload best.
verify.teamwork.polite: Read the message aloud: does it sound like you? Remove phrases you wouldn't say.
verify.teamwork.help: Asking for help is normal. Check your request makes clear exactly what you need and how long it'll take.
verify.teamwork.feedback: Good feedback is about the work, not the person. Check the text has no judgements about character.
verify.teamwork.disagree: The goal is to solve the problem, not to win. Check the text leaves room for the other view.
verify.teamwork.summary: A summary should reflect what was said, not what you wish had been said. Ask a participant to check it.
verify.teamwork.open: Not every open question needs settling now. Mark which ones are blocking work.
verify.teamwork.recipient: Don't put anyone's contact details or personal information in the prompt. Describe the recipient by role.
